scenes.vo: risk-adjusted yield equals headline minus (annual loss probability times loss given default) minus costs You don't know the true loss probability, so write down an assumption and be conservative. Newer protocols, more dependencies and higher leverage deserve higher numbers. The point isn't precision; it's making you compare positions on the same footing.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: the calculator The 9% vault still wins on expectation, but by 2 points, not 4.5. Its bad outcome is also far worse, so size it smaller (Lesson 13.3). New protocol vault, 9.0%, 3% a year, 100%, 6.0%. Blue-chip lending, 4.5%, 0.5% a year, 100%, 4.0%.

scenes.vo: Question one. 12% headline, 5% a year loss probability, 60% LGD. Risk-adjusted? [[pause 4]] The answer: 12 minus 3 equals 9%.
scenes.cap: Question 1. 12% headline, 5%/yr loss probability, 60% LGD. Risk-adjusted? The answer: 12 − 3 = 9%.

scenes.a: Losses cluster in stress, when many positions fail together; optimistic assumptions overstate income.

scenes.q: Two positions, same risk-adjusted yield. Which gets more capital?
scenes.a: The one with the smaller and better-understood worst case.
